title: URPX Utility Discovery Manifest
description: Per-utility manifest at <country>/<subdivision>/<utility>/utility.toml, e.g. us/ca/pge/utility.toml. Points to where the utility publishes its tariffs so that scrapers can discover unmodeled schedules and detect updates to modeled ones. Distinct from the per-filing tariff.toml: tariff.toml pins a specific snapshot (URL + sha256 + retrieval date), utility.toml points at the discovery surface where future snapshots can be found. It also carries the utility's identity, which generators previously held as python literals: a display name, the regulatory class, the legal name and EIA identifier, and the MIDAS party segments and party names. One authoritative place on disk, read through dev/utilities.py. Identity fields other than utility_class are optional because the repository cannot attest all of them for every party: legal_name and eia_id are taken from the corpus JSON-LD where a filing exists, and on a manifest-only utility only where the manifest cites a source; dev/lint_utility_manifests.py holds both to the filings once there are any.

utility.description: Short identifier matching the directory name (e.g. 'pge', 'cpau', 'sdcp'). dev/lint_utility_manifests.py enforces the match; this schema cannot, because it never sees where the file sits.

tariff_index_urls.description: One or more URLs where the utility publishes tariffs. Each should be a discovery surface, of which three kinds matter: a tariff library or book (where a schedule's current document is fetched), an advice-letter listing (what says a change happened), and a schedule inventory (what says which schedules exist and which are grandfathered or closed). A discovery surface is often a PDF, so being a PDF does not disqualify one: SCE's annual summary of available rates is a schedule inventory. What does not belong is a single schedule's tariff, which is pinned in that filing's tariff.toml instead.

scrape_notes.description: Free-text hints about scrape strategy: known TLS-fingerprint blocks (curl_cffi required), URL patterns per schedule, AL-listing locations, paywalls, etc.

utility_class.description: Regulatory class: investor-owned utility, publicly owned utility, or community choice aggregator. ASSERTED, not derived: MIDAS carries no classification and distinguishes these only accidentally, through whether the distribution half of a party segment names a utility or reads XX. Required, because it is knowable for every party here and was previously held in three places with three different vocabularies.

short_name.description: Display name for report headings, e.g. 'PG&E'. Optional: only supplied where an abbreviation is established, which in practice means the utilities that have filings. dev/utilities.py refuses if a utility with filings lacks one, so a new modeled utility cannot silently fall out of a per-utility report.

legal_name.description: The utility's legal name as the corpus itself states it in urpx:legalName. Recorded here so that generators stop carrying their own spellings; four different spellings of the same three utilities were in circulation.

eia_id.description: EIA utility identifier, the skos:notation on this utility's urpx:OrganizationIdentifier under urpx:eiaScheme. A stable join key against the EIA-861 detailed data files. A string rather than an integer because it is a notation, not a quantity.

midas_party_names.description: How the CEC MIDAS Energy lookup table spells this party's Description. An array because an organization can appear under more than one. Used to attribute MIDAS rows to a directory; absent where MIDAS does not carry the party at all, which is the case for CPAU.

midas_bundled_segment.description: The four-character MIDAS party segment for this utility's own bundled service, where both delivery and generation are its own (e.g. 'PGPG'). Absent where MIDAS carries no bundled segment for the party.

midas_delivery_segment.description: The MIDAS party segment for delivery-only service, where generation comes from a community choice aggregator (e.g. 'PGXX'). A publicly owned utility has no community choice aggregation in its territory and so has none; verified against the mined feed, where the POU delivery-only forms return zero rows.

delivered_by.description: The utility slug whose wires carry this party's generation, for a community choice aggregator. Absent means the party delivers over its own wires. A slug rather than a display name so it resolves against a directory.
